approach.method_basis: GenMol generates by remasking rather than by building from scratch. A bidirectional masked diffusion model is trained to fill in deleted spans of a molecular fragment sequence, so at generation time you take an existing molecule, blank out one fragment, and let the model iteratively denoise the gap while every surrounding fragment stays fixed. Because the model sees context on both sides, the replacement it writes has to fit what remains, which keeps the output chemically coherent in a way left-to-right generation does not guarantee.
approach.novelty: This root commits to a fragment representation with explicit attachment labels that are round-trip checked during preparation, so the retained context keeps its exact connection points and the replacement block must satisfy them. It freezes the denoiser entirely and adapts per objective only by changing which observed molecules are selected to supply future contexts, ranked by their accepted scores. All learning is therefore in the choice of what to remask, not in the model that fills the gap.

observed_bottleneck: This root has no Parent. The benchmark difficulty is to convert a small task-local set of scored molecules into useful new structures with limited feedback. The supplied observation n-4fa9546e559e confirms that graph evolution generated valid novel offspring and reused feedback, but most evaluated offspring did not exceed their best generating parent. That motivates measuring whether learned conditional fragment replacement can preserve useful molecular context while proposing improving alternatives; it does not establish a diffusion-specific failure or a comparative score advantage. The central untested prerequisite is useful conditional generation from a compact denoiser trained only on the permitted unlabeled corpus.
hypothesis: Freeze a corpus-trained bidirectional masked discrete denoiser over SAFE fragment sequences, then repeatedly select high-ranked task-local observed molecules, replace one fragment with a variable-length mask chunk, iteratively denoise the missing tokens while preserving the surrounding context, and use accepted scores to update which whole molecules supply future contexts.

finding_summary.headline: Second highest at 0.495, and the most consistent root across all five objectives
finding_summary.insights: Consistency, not peak performance, is what this node contributes. Its sitagliptin_mpo score of 0.344 is the best in the round and its drd2_docking of 0.908 is third, which no other method combines. The negative context-beating delta is the interesting result: the search improves by keeping the rare good completion and discarding the rest, rather than by proposing better molecules on average. That means throughput of attempts matters more here than proposal quality, which is a different tuning direction from every other lineage. One seed, and the fragment vocabulary itself has not been varied.
finding_summary.results: The macro mean of 0.495 is second of thirteen. It is the only root above 0.20 on every single objective: 0.908 on drd2_docking, 0.591 on deco_hop, 0.424 on zaleplon_mpo, 0.344 on sitagliptin_mpo and 0.207 on median_2. Context selection enrichment was positive on every objective and held under a tie-midrank sensitivity check. Every remasking attempt decoded with an unchanged prefix and suffix, a nonempty retained subgraph, exactly one replacement block and fixed outside attachment labels. One registered measurement came back against expectation: the mean score of a completion minus its generating context is negative in aggregate and on every task, so individual completions usually score worse than the molecule they came from.

molecular.headline: The cleanest and most consistent chemistry in the round, anchored on one xanthine-like core
molecular.overall_character: Ring closure and aromatic content both reach 100 percent on two objectives and never fall below 98 percent, and cumulated double bonds are effectively absent throughout. The molecules read as coherent medicinal chemistry with correct attachment: pyrazolines, sulfonyl pyrrolidines, halogenated benzoates. Fragment remasking preserves whatever was already there, which shows as a strong shared core across objectives, a dimethyl pyrimidinedione appearing in the top molecules of three of them. Halogen content is high at 48 to 95 percent, and molecule size stays moderate at forty-three to seventy characters.

per_task.generated_character: Phenyl pyrazolines bearing a thiourea or thiocarbamate, averaging forty-three characters, fully ring-closed with 99 percent aromatic content.
liabilities: N-chloro thiourea groups are both reactive and toxicologically unacceptable
chloroacetyl is an alkylating group that would not be advanced
missing_features: alternatives to the thiourea linkage carried by every top scorer
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top four share one pyrazoline thiourea core, scoring 0.395 to 0.424, and the difference between them is where a chloroacetyl sits on the pendant ring. At the bottom are fully saturated sugar-like acetonides that score zero, which the remasking would only reach if the context molecule was already off-target.

per_task.generated_character: Aryl-substituted pyrimidinediones averaging fifty-eight characters, with aromatic content and ring closure both at exactly 100 percent and a 64 percent halogen rate.
liabilities: terminal alkyne and enyne tails in several top scorers are metabolically reactive
a carbodiimide-like C=N terminus recurs across the top of the range
missing_features: scaffold variation beyond the single pyrimidinedione core carried by all top scorers
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The band is tight, 0.564 median against 0.591 best, and every one of the top four carries the same fluorinated dimethyl pyrimidinedione with a pendant pyridine. The variation is confined to the ether tail, which is precisely what remasking one fragment on a fixed context produces.

per_task.generated_character: Sulfonyl pyrrolidines carrying a diamine chain to a substituted aryl, averaging seventy characters, 95 percent halogenated and entirely ring-closed.
liabilities: aryl sulfonyl pyrrolidines are heavy and metabolically exposed at this substitution level
missing_features: the compact indole ethylamine that reached above 0.97 in two other roots
smaller molecules; this population averages seventy characters where the winners average forty
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top four are one architecture with the halogen pattern and the linker length varied, spanning 0.805 to 0.908, and every one carries a secondary amine in the middle of the chain. The near-zero molecules are flat coumarins and open amino acids with the basic nitrogen removed, which again identifies the basic amine as the scoring feature.

per_task.generated_character: Benzodioxole-substituted pyrimidinediones averaging sixty-two characters, with aromatic content and ring closure both at exactly 100 percent, the cleanest set on this objective in the round.
liabilities: conjugated diyne chains in the low scorers are unstable
missing_features: a second scaffold family; every scorer above 0.19 shares one core
molecules balancing the two similarity targets rather than resembling one
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best at 0.207 leads this objective across all thirteen roots, and the top four are the same benzodioxole pyrimidinedione with the ester and the ring substituent varied. The lowest scorers keep the same core but replace the aryl with alkyl and alkyne chains, which costs about half the score.

per_task.generated_character: The best result any root achieved on this objective. Compact halogenated benzoates fused to a dimethyl pyrimidinedione, averaging fifty-three characters with 73 percent halogenation and 98 percent aromatic content.
missing_features: aliphatic fluorinated chemistry rather than halogen on aromatic rings
stereochemistry, absent from every proposal on every objective
a second scaffold family to test against the single pyrimidinedione core
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The top four are the same molecule with fluorine, chlorine and bromine permuted around one benzoate ring, spanning 0.334 to 0.344, while the median across all 290 proposals is 0.004. The search found one narrow answer and refined its halogen pattern, which is exactly what fragment remasking on a fixed context does.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The registered context-beating measurement is negative in aggregate and on every one of the five objectives, meaning the average child underperforms its own parent context, yet the incumbent still improves through selection.
transferable_gaps.gap: individual completions score worse than the molecule they were derived from
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator is not a proposal improver; it is a lottery whose winners are kept. That makes attempt throughput and context ranking the levers that matter, and makes any change aimed at raising average proposal quality the wrong place to spend effort.

transferable_gaps.evidence: A dimethyl pyrimidinedione appears in the top-scoring molecules of three separate objectives, and on two of them the top four differ only by which halogen sits on one ring.
transferable_gaps.gap: the generator preserves so much context that one core dominates every objective
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Remasking a single fragment while fixing every attachment label cannot leave the neighbourhood of the starting molecule. Reaching a different core needs either multi-fragment remasking or occasional context resets that discard the current archive.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The highest-scoring molecule on one objective carries both an N-chloro thiourea and a chloroacetyl group, and thiourea appears in all four top scorers there.
transferable_gaps.gap: the generator writes reactive and toxic functional groups into completions
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The denoiser learned these tokens from the corpus and the reward has no way to object, so they persist wherever they happen to score. A toxicophore screen at emission removes them without touching the denoiser or the selection rule.

method_name: GenMol fragment remasking with a corpus-trained discrete denoiser
method_thesis: Anchor the method in GenMol's fragment-remasking mechanism: a bidirectional masked discrete diffusion model generates replacement fragments while retaining the surrounding molecular context. The anchor is described in [GenMol, Sections 4.1-4.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2501.06158v3). For this benchmark adaptation, train a compact denoiser solely on the permitted unlabeled corpus, then freeze it. Start each objective with a fresh archive of its supplied scored molecules. Select high-ranked observed whole molecules as contexts, replace a randomly chosen fragment with a variable-length mask chunk, iteratively sample the missing SAFE tokens, and decode the resulting complete molecule. Generate further completions until the evaluator-announced batch contains distinct canonical structures. Accepted feedback updates context selection and allows improving completions to become future contexts. This root uses the remasking core with observed whole-molecule contexts; the paper's corpus-derived fragment-vocabulary initialization and fragment-attaching stage are not required. The corpus trains the denoiser and supplies unlabeled length statistics, never a molecule pool for ranking or retrieval. The hypothesis is that contextual fragment replacement preserves useful structure while generating improving alternatives, raising the mean of the five independent final Top-1 scores. Task-local selection can respond immediately to feedback without reward-dependent neural training, but useful conditional generation from the permitted preparation remains an empirical prerequisite.
